Comet builder — a SF_KINDS.COMET body is a dark
Source src/experiments/star-field/engine/bodies/comet.ts
UX surface Boot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

SF_USER_GAS

userData key each tail InstancedMesh node uses to stash its particle simulation record: the live position/color Float32Arrays, the instance-buffer handles (aMat = instanceMatrix, aCol = instanceColor — so updateFx can flag needsUpdate), the seeded per-grain vectors (emission phase, lateral offset, stream rate, wobble, size jitter), and the layer's base dimensions (tail length, root spread, fan growth, grain size, tint, opacity). Storing the arrays here — rather than reading them back out of buffers — keeps the frame loop allocation-free AND makes the record inspectable without a live three.js renderer.

tailLayer

Builds ONE comet-tail particle layer: an InstancedMesh of n billboarded glow quads plus the simulation record updateFx animates. Each grain i cycles d = frac(phase[i] + t·rate[i]) — d=0 is fresh emission hugging the nucleus, d=1 is fully dispersed — and updateFx maps it to x = d·len anti-sunward with a lateral offset lat[i]·spread·(1+grow·d) (the tail widens downstream as solar-wind pressure disperses it) plus a seeded sinusoidal wobble (plasma turbulence) and a z-offset (real depth — the sheet reads volumetric, not painted). Per-grain brightness dim[i]·envelope(d) rides in the instance-color channel: the ramp smoothstep keeps the root from popping in as a wall, and the (1−d)^fade decay makes every grain die at its own distance — the aggregate tip is a ragged dissolve, never a straight line.

Why instanced quads and not THREE.Points: under the WebGPU node pipeline PointsMaterial.size is not honored the way WebGL's gl_PointSize is — grains rasterize at a pixel or two regardless of the requested world size, so a real volumetric tail renders as confetti. An InstancedMesh of unit quads — one draw call for the whole cloud, each instance matrix billboarded onto the camera orientation per frame — keeps real world-space size, the soft glow texture, and per-grain HDR color on every renderer.

(module scope)

Pseudo-normal lateral offset — the mean of three uniforms concentrates density on the spine while still filling a diffuse sheath, so the column is denser down its axis like a real tail (a flat [-1,1] draw would smear the brightness evenly).

quad

Unit quad instanced per grain — instance color carries the grain's brightness (MeshBasicMaterial multiplies the map by instanceColor, and additive blending turns dim color into transparency, so per-grain fade needs no shader). The buffers are DynamicDraw — updateFx rewrites both every frame.

(module scope)

rgb is the layer tint decomposed to floats — updateFx writes col[i] = rgb·env(i,d) per frame without allocating a Color; aMat/aCol alias the instance buffers so needsUpdate reaches the GPU side without touching geometry internals.

makeComet

Builds the comet composite: an irregular, nearly-black nucleus (the real Halley albedo is ~0.04 — one of the darkest known bodies), a soft additive coma sprite hugging it, and the ion + dust particle tails. The nucleus mesh becomes the node's mesh/spinner so it tumbles normally; coma rides inside it (a symmetric billboard is indifferent to spin); the tails mount on center where local +x is permanently anti-sunward. Each tail is two particle layers — a tight bright core stream and a wide dim sheath — so the column reads as a volume of gas with a dense spine, not a painted band.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry — radius sizes the nucleus AND every tail
  • @param texMap Loaded texture map (a comet with a real nucleus map
  • @param glowTex Shared radial-glow texture — used for the coma sprite
  • @returns { mesh, coma, ion, dust, ionGas, dustGas } — the pickable

ion

Ion tail — long, narrow, fast-streaming plasma column. Two layers: the core grains are small/bright (the dense spine) and the sheath grains are large/dim (the diffuse gas envelope the spine rides in).

dust

Dust tail — shorter, broader, slower: grains retain orbital momentum so the fan trails the radius vector (the DUST_TILT lag) and disperses wider than the magnetically-locked ion stream.
